episodes.213731: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved northeast across the area during the evening hours of June 30th. One thunderstorm produced large hail near the Colorado border.
episodes.213780: A strong thunderstorm briefly generated high winds near the town of Oacoma during the early morning hours of July 1. A peak wind gust of 64 mph (56 knots) was recorded by the South Dakota State University mesonet station one mile west of Oacoma.
episodes.213807: During the afternoon and evening of July 1, numerous westward and northwestward-moving storms formed across mainly the northern half of Central Alabama. These storms produced numerous instances of tree damage along with several reports of hail. Notably, golf ball-size hail fell in Hokes Bluff in Etowah County. The next two days featured thunderstorm activity mainly across Blount and Etowah counties, with minor damage, along with minor flooding in Homewood in Jefferson County.
episodes.213847: The surface boundary that was present on June 29th continued to remain across the region into the 30th. Additional showers and thunderstorms developed again on the afternoon and evening of the 30th. Damaging winds were the primary hazard with these storms are enough dry air aloft was able to bring down stronger winds in any robust thunderstorm.
episodes.213945: Warm temperatures combined with sufficient mid level moisture, wind energy, and an approaching weather disturbance to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of July 1st, especially across portions of the southern Texas Panhandle. Some of these were able to become strong to severe with damaging winds being the primary hazard. Slow movement of storms along with efficient heavy rainfall allowed for some flash flooding to occur.
episodes.214134: A weak dryline formed during the day of the 30th and mixed eastward to the edge of the caprock. Convergence along the dryline, a weak short wave trough, and very hot temperatures contributed to convective initiation by mid-afternoon across the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle and northern Rolling Plains. Storms repeatedly trained over Hall County producing intermittent severe winds gusts near Lesley (Hall County) for over an hour. Late in the afternoon additional thunderstorms developed in eastern New Mexico in the drier air and moved eastward into the South Plains. A very dry sub cloud layer allowed these storms to produce several severe wind gusts as they marched eastward towards the Interstate 27/US Highway 87 corridor. By the time storms reached Lubbock County late in the evening, they were moving very slowly which produced heavy rainfall over the city of Lubbock (Lubbock County). Numerous city roads on the south side of the city of Lubbock were inundated with water.
episodes.214170: A shortwave moving across the area (coupled with upslope flow) led to the development of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across west Texas and southeast New Mexico. A couple of storms producing severe winds, and one produced damage to power poles near Monument, NM.
episodes.214171: A shortwave moving across the area (coupled with upslope flow) led to the development of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across west Texas and southeast New Mexico. A couple of storms producing severe winds, and one produced damage to power poles near Monument, NM.
episodes.214492: A supercell thunderstorm produce 2 tornadoes severe hail and wind gusts up to 74 mph.
episodes.214662: A typical summertime pattern produced scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms with isolated severe weather reported.
episodes.214663: The area was the western periphery of a broad area of high pressure.  A sea breeze boundary moved inland and encountered a warm and unstable airmass resulting in thunderstorm development.  A thunderstorm in Jackson County produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.215407: Storms blossomed in the right entrance region of an upper level jet across northern Nebraska into southeast South Dakota during the very early morning hours of July 1.  Plentiful instability up to 3000 J/kg was available to a 40-60 knot low-level jet, and storms fired along a distinct west to east band which progressed slowly northward through the overnight.  Winds from 60 to 80 mph were common with considerable tree damage in many areas.
episodes.215409: Storms blossomed in the right entrance region of an upper level jet across northern Nebraska into southeast South Dakota during the very early morning hours of July 1.  Plentiful instability up to 3000 J/kg was available to a 40-60 knot low-level jet, and storms fired along a distinct west to east band which progressed slowly northward through the overnight. episodes.215421: On June 30, 2026, a cold front extending from Minnesota into east-central Nebraska and southwest Iowa interacted with an extremely unstable air mass featuring SBCAPE exceeding 4,000 J/kg. Strong capping suppressed widespread convection during the evening, allowing only a single storm to develop in southwest Iowa. This storm produced a measured 58 mph wind gust in Mills County and caused damage to a garage door and machine shed in Pottawattamie County before weakening late in the evening.
episodes.215422: During the overnight hours of June 30 into July 1, 2026, a cold front extending from Minnesota into east-central Nebraska and southwest Iowa interacted with an extremely unstable air mass featuring SBCAPE exceeding 4,000 J/kg. Strong capping suppressed activity through much of the evening. Overnight, an approaching shortwave disturbance combined with an intensifying low-level jet and increasing vertical shear to erode the cap, triggering a complex of severe thunderstorms. This convective line tracked across far northeast Nebraska, where a 62 mph wind gust was measured near Crofton at 12:58 AM CST on July 1, before moving north into southeastern South Dakota and northwestern Iowa.
episodes.215522: On June 30, 2026, an oppressive tropical airmass fueled by extreme heat warnings collided with a sharp mid-level shortwave across the NWS Buffalo CWA, prompting the Storm Prediction Center to issue a Severe Thunderstorm Watch as strong boundary-layer destabilization produced widespread severe convection across Central New York and the North Country. NWS Buffalo Area Forecast Discussions highlighted surging moisture and extreme instability that unleashed powerful multi-cell clusters and isolated supercells, leading to severe straight-line microbursts with winds up to 100 mph and an EF-1 tornado touchdown in Lewis County. Concurrently, deep warm-cloud processes and precipitable water levels approaching 2.0 inches fueled torrential precipitation efficiency, driving Weather Prediction Center Excessive Rainfall concerns for localized flash flooding in poor-drainage areas. As the pre-frontal convective line swept east toward nightfall, loss of daytime heating and post-frontal drying rapidly stabilized the region, bringing an end to the severe weather threat into the overnight hours.
episodes.215587: Thunderstorms moving through Saginaw Bay and southern Lake Huron produced wind gusts  in excess of 40 knots.
episodes.215627: A few thunderstorms moved northeast into southern Yuma County during the early to mid-evening hours on the 30th. The thunderstorms produced quarter size hail and an estimated 60 mph wind gust west of Bonny Lake.
episodes.215706: During the evening hours on the 30th, a few clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved northeast across portions of west-central and northwest Kansas. An 81 mph wind gust was measured in Wichita County.
episodes.215890: High heat and humidity amid an abnormally warm airmass and ample sunshine made for highly unstable conditions across eastern New York on July 1st and 2nd, 2026. Severe thunderstorms, forced by sufficiently robust mid- to upper-level shortwaves cresting the top of a significant ridge, consequently developed in the mid- to late-evening on both days. On July 1st, convection erupted just after 4 PM and lingered through close to 11 PM. The scattered nature of the storms led to widespread impacts noted in the Adirondacks, Mohawk Valley, Upper-Hudson Valley, Capital District, Mid-Hudson Valley, Taconics, and Mid-Hudson Valley. While some small hail was noted within a few storms, the primary hazard was wind damage. Numerous reports of downed trees and wires were therefore forwarded to NWS Albany. On July 2nd, one cluster of storms in particular developed just before 9 PM, and in reaching severe strength, led to severe tree damage in Columbia County. In fact, the town of Chatham declared a State of Emergency due to the extensive damage that led to more than 40 service calls throughout the overnight. Numerous roads were closed due to blockages from downed trees and wires, many were without power also as a result of downed trees; wires; and damaged transformers, and some in the village even lost water as the water pump station lost power and the backup generator failed. The extent of damage in Chatham led to the determination that this cluster produced winds in excess of 60 mph, with some gusts likely getting as high as 70-90 mph.
episodes.215928: Additional clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed along the edges of a high-pressure ridge extending from the Great Lakes and Canada into the northern portions of the region. High dew points and sufficient instability supported scattered thunderstorms that produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215970: Severe thunderstorms over northeastern Colorado and the southern Nebraska Panhandle moved east into southwestern Nebraska during the late evening hours of June 30th. This activity continued into the early morning hours of July 1st tracking across the Sandhills into north central Nebraska.  Strong damaging winds up to 85 MPH were reported at Kingsley Dam.  There were several 60 to 80 MPH wind gusts reported over southwestern Nebraska.
episodes.215971: Severe thunderstorms tracked across the central Sandhills into north central Nebraska during the early morning hours of July 1st. Several thunderstorm wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH were reported. Even stronger wind gusts between 70 and 80 MPH were reported in Thomas, Rock and Boyd Counties.
episodes.216035: Outflow boundaries from robust convection over the southern Everglades propagated southward across Florida Bay and the Nearshore Gulf Waters.  Subsequent thunderstorm development along these boundaries produced wind gusts of 30 to 35 knots across large portions of the Florida Keys coastal waters.
episodes.216123: Additional clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed along the edges of a high-pressure ridge extending from the Great Lakes and Canada into the northern portions of the region. High dew points and sufficient instability supported scattered thunderstorms that produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.216128: Afternoon convection within deep layer easterly sea breeze flow produces a few strong marine wind gusts across Tampa Bay.
episodes.216668: A wave of precipitation during the morning continued ongoing minor flood impacts in the Many Glacier area of Glacier National Park. Another disturbance moved through in the afternoon, bringing good instability and a high moisture content for thunderstorms. Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms lead to minor flash flooding in Bozeman.
episodes.216691: A strong upper ridge was centered over the Ohio River Valley and central Appalachians during the morning of July 1, 2026. A weak shortwave moved westward from Georgia and Alabama, along the southern periphery of the upper ridge, and into Mississippi. This feature combined with moderate instability (MLCAPEs around 2000 J/kg) to trigger diurnal  thunderstorms over northeast Mississippi during the late afternoon and early evening. Several instances of damaging winds occurred.
episodes.216709: During the morning hours on July 1st, a trained spotter reported a 59 mph wind gust as storms moved through the area.
episodes.216726: An upper level ridge of high pressure built in across the Ozarks into the Mid-South Region to start the first day of July, resulting in an easterly flow aloft across the Four State Region. A weak upper level disturbance drifted west beneath the ridge during the afternoon of the 1st, which provided increased large scale forcing in an area where strong instability had developed given the afternoon temperatures in the lower to mid 90s, and ample low level moisture. As a result, scattered showers and thunderstorms, some of which were severe, developed across portions of North Louisiana, producing damaging winds which downed trees and power lines before diminishing during the evening with the loss of heating and instability.
episodes.216749: A moist, weakly forced summertime environment persisted across southeast Louisiana on July 1st as the upper ridge shifted slightly northeast of the region and the previous night's easterly disturbance increased moisture across the area. Scattered convection developed along coastal and mesoscale boundaries by midday. A waterspout developed over the marsh and coastal waters near Hopedale and Delacroix.
episodes.216750: A moist, weakly forced summertime environment persisted across southeast Louisiana on July 1st as the upper ridge shifted slightly northeast of the region and the previous night's easterly disturbance increased moisture across the area. Lightning from ongoing thunderstorms struck a home and started a fire. The home was reported to be a total loss.
episodes.216810: As an upper level ridge broke down across the region, scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed with one storm becoming severe.
episodes.216821: During the morning hours of July 1st, severe storms moved through portions of west-central Wisconsin and caused several instances of tree damage.
episodes.216867: Locally induced afternoon thunderstorms over northwestern Puerto Rico during the first week of July produced strong gusts and, a funnel cloud was sighted.
episodes.216873: The Storm Prediction Center highlighted parts of Western New York under a Marginal to Slight Risk for severe weather on July 1st, citing an unstable air mass ahead of an approaching cold front. NWS Buffalo's Area Forecast Discussions noted that daytime heating in the 80s combined with pooling dew points near 70��F to generate moderate surface-based instability across the CWA. Convection initialized along early afternoon lake breeze boundaries before organizing into multi-cell line segments along the primary frontal boundary. As storms moved west to east, the primary hazards observed across the Finger Lakes and Eastern Great Lake regions were localized damaging wind gusts along with isolated heavy downpours.
